# Claude Desktop Theme Tuner: a guide for AI agents

The tuner themes the Claude desktop app. A theme is 13 colors per mode
(light and dark). The tuner shows a live preview of Claude in those colors
and writes a DevTools snippet that the user runs in Claude to apply it.

You never need to click through the page. Describe a theme as JSON, put it in
a link, and open or screenshot the link.

App: https://rinn7e.com/claude-desktop-theme-tuner/
Source (MIT): https://github.com/rinn7e/claude-desktop-theme-tuner

## The link

    https://rinn7e.com/claude-desktop-theme-tuner/#theme=<JSON, URI-encoded>

Add `&view=preview` to show only the preview of Claude, for screenshots. It
fills the window up to 1280px wide, so a window at least 700px wide shows the
whole mock. Without it, the link opens the full tuner with the theme loaded,
ready for the user to copy the snippet.

The JSON:

    {
      "light": {
        "preset": "solarized-light",
        "name": "Neon Solarized",
        "colors": { "accent": "#c0009f", "accentHover": "#a3008a" }
      },
      "dark": { "preset": "dracula" },
      "reduceMotion": false
    }

- `light`, `dark`: each optional. A mode left out stays as Claude ships it.
- `preset`: a preset id (below) to start from. Optional.
- `colors`: overrides the preset's colors, as `#rrggbb`. Without a `preset`,
  all 13 colors are required.
- `name`: shown in the tuner and in the snippet. Optional.
- `reduceMotion`: true also turns off Claude's looping animations.

Build the link with encodeURIComponent, for example:

    node -e 'const theme = {light: {preset: "solarized-light", colors: {accent: "#c0009f"}}}; console.log("https://rinn7e.com/claude-desktop-theme-tuner/#theme=" + encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify(theme)) + "&view=preview")'

## The 13 colors

Surfaces:
- `frame`: sidebar, title bar, menus
- `canvas`: chat area, composer, panes
- `raised`: cards, inputs
- `pressed`: hovered and stronger fills

Text:
- `text`: messages, titles
- `textSecondary`: labels, list rows, Claude's thinking and tool rows
- `textMuted`: hints, timestamps

Accent and lines:
- `accent`: links, buttons, focus rings, progress bars
- `accentHover`: the hovered accent
- `onAccent`: text and icons on accent buttons
- `line`: borders, applied at 22% and 40% opacity

Lists and washes:
- `selected`: the selected sidebar row; hover uses it at 27%
- `wash`: the user's message bubbles and neutral tints, applied at 10%

## Rules for a good theme

Contrast is WCAG contrast ratio. The tuner's own presets all pass these:

- `text`, `textSecondary` and `textMuted` at least 4.5 on both `canvas` and
  `frame`.
- `accent` at least 4.5 on `canvas`: one color serves both links and buttons,
  so a bright neon must be darkened to work as link text. Use the bright shade
  for `accentHover` or `selected` instead, where it is not text.
- `onAccent` at least 4.5 on `accent`.
- `text` at least 4.5 on `selected`, and `selected` clearly visible against
  `frame` (about 1.15 or more).
- `textSecondary` dimmer than `text`, at least 1.5 apart, so Claude's thinking
  reads apart from its replies; `textMuted` no brighter than `textSecondary`.
- `raised` and `pressed` visibly different from `canvas` and `frame`.

The full tuner (the link without `&view=preview`) shows these checks for the
current theme.

## Presets

Every preset's 13 colors, as JSON, to start from or to check contrast
against without a browser:

    https://rinn7e.com/claude-desktop-theme-tuner/presets.json

    [{ "id": "solarized-light", "name": "Solarized Light", "mode": "light",
       "palette": { "frame": "#eee8d5", "canvas": "#fdf6e3", ... } }, ...]

The ids:

Light: claude-light, github-light, pierre-light, vs-code-light, one-light,
catppuccin-latte, solarized-light, vitesse-light, min-light, rose-pine-dawn,
slack-ochin, gruvbox-light, meadow-light

Dark: claude-dark, github-dark, github-dark-dimmed, pierre-dark, vs-code-dark,
one-dark, dracula, dracula-soft, catppuccin-mocha, nord, solarized-dark,
vitesse-dark, min-dark, monokai, tokyo-night, night-owl, rose-pine, ayu-dark,
slack-dark, gruvbox-dark, groovy-lambda-black

## Screenshots

With a browser tool, open the `&view=preview` link and wait for an element
with the `data-ready` attribute. From a shell, Playwright does it in one
command:

    npx playwright screenshot --wait-for-selector "[data-ready]" --full-page "<link>" theme-1.png

If it fails because Playwright's browser is not installed, either install it
once with `npx playwright install chromium` (a one-time download) or open the links
in your browser tool instead. In a browser tool, navigate to each link and
take a screenshot; never fill in the color fields one by one.

## Recipe: "design me a theme"

1. Pick a starting preset from the user's request (its colors are in
   presets.json), or write all 13 colors.
2. Design the variants the user asked for, keeping the rules above.
3. Build one `&view=preview` link per variant and screenshot each.
4. Show the user the screenshots, each with its link without `&view=preview`.
5. The user opens the one they like. The tuner loads it and explains how to
   apply it: copy the snippet, then run it in Claude's DevTools (Help >
   Troubleshooting > Enable Developer Mode). Applying it is the user's step,
   since it runs code in their Claude app.
